subject.title: chore(deps): bump the actions group across 1 directory with 14 updates

question: Should OpenClaw accept these 14 executable Action updates as one reviewed batch after exact-head validation, or split the credential-bearing Codex, app-token, CodeQL, and Docker updates into separately attributable PRs?
rationale: Several updated actions run with secrets or write-capable tokens, and their release or dispatch paths are not fully exercised by routine pull-request CI, so accepting the grouped supply-chain change requires human ownership judgment.

options.title: Refresh and approve the batch
options.body: Rebase or refresh Dependabot, review upstream changes, and run or inspect exact-head smoke evidence for each credential-bearing workflow family before merging.

options.title: Split sensitive action families
options.body: Separate Codex, GitHub App token, CodeQL/SARIF, and Docker publishing action updates so failures and security review are independently attributable.

options.title: Accept current grouped risk
options.body: Merge the full-SHA batch after owner review while accepting that some scheduled and release-only paths receive their first real exercise after landing.

recommendation.title: Refresh and approve the batch
recommendation.body: Rebase or refresh Dependabot, review upstream changes, and run or inspect exact-head smoke evidence for each credential-bearing workflow family before merging.

likelyOwner.reason: The history shows the strongest cross-cutting ownership of action modernization and the affected agent and release workflows.
